events.text: Bandits on the road home. Before you can draw, {npc} is already standing at your shoulder, sleeves rolled up.

mem.note: fought back to back with me

ok.log: It is over in a minute. {npc} laughs the whole way home. You have never loved {him} more.

mem.note: fought back to back with me

fail.log: You win, barely, both bleeding. {npc} bandages you and scolds you for being slow.

mem.note: treated me like I could not fight

effects.log: {npc} stays back, and is quiet for the rest of the evening. Some people do not want to be protected.

events.text: It is the anniversary of your wedding. {npc} pretends not to remember, which means {he} remembers perfectly.

choices.text: Take {him} to the place you first met

effects.log: The teahouse is smaller than you remember. The tea is worse. It is a perfect evening.

choices.text: Give a gift you made yourself

mem.note: made me a gift with their own hands

effects.log: It is a little crooked. {npc} keeps it beside the bed for the rest of {his} life.

events.text: {npc} has a fever that will not break. The village physician only sighs.

ok.log: Three nights of needles and herbs. On the fourth morning {npc} asks for congee. You cry into the pot.

mem.note: never left my side when I was ill

fail.log: Your medicine is not enough, but you never leave {his} side, and the fever breaks on its own. Neither of you forgets those nights.

choices.text: Pay for the best physician in the capital

mem.note: brought the best physician for me

effects.log: Fifty taels and a carriage. The physician arrives in time.

events.text: {npc} wants something of {his} own: to open a school, train fighters, be more than someone's husband or wife.

effects.log: The school opens in spring. Within a year, it has more students than you expected, and {npc} is happier than you have ever seen.

choices.text: Ask {him} to wait a few years

mem.note: asked me to wait for my own life

effects.log: {npc} agrees, and does not mention it again. You notice.

events.text: A quarrel over nothing becomes a quarrel over everything. {npc} sleeps in the other room.

effects.log: It costs you nothing but pride. By morning you are laughing about it.
Three days of silence. Then {npc} apologises, and you wish you had gone first.

events.text: {npc}'s whole family descends for the New Year: parents, aunts, cousins, and an uncle who wants to test your sword.

ok.log: The uncle bows after the third exchange, and spends the rest of the visit telling everyone you are the family's favourite.

fail.log: The uncle wins, then spends the evening telling everyone. {npc} cannot stop laughing.

effects.log: Thirty people, one kitchen, and a feast nobody will forget. The uncle forgets the test.

events.text: {npc} falls asleep against your shoulder by the fire, as {he} has done for years.

mem.note: let me sleep on their shoulder all night

effects.log: Your shoulder is numb by dawn. You would not trade it for a realm.
{npc} wakes halfway and pretends not to. You both know.

events.text: {npc} has made a wooden sword and wants you to watch the forms {he} invented.

effects.log: Fourteen forms, all named after animals. You learn more about your child than about swords.
{npc} listens, then does it your way, then does it {his} own way again. Good.

events.text: {npc} comes home with a split lip and will not say who did it.

mem.note: taught me to stand up for myself

effects.log: Two weeks of training. The next time, nobody touches {npc}, and {npc} does not touch anyone either. Good.
A long, cold conversation. The bullying stops. {npc} is embarrassed and grateful in equal parts.

events.text: {npc} wants to join a sect you never liked.

mem.note: let me choose my own road

effects.log: {npc} goes. Letters come every month. {He} becomes someone you are proud of.
{npc} obeys. Something between you closes, quietly.

events.text: {npc} has run off to the city with friends and your best horse.

effects.log: The silence on the road home is worse than any shouting. It works.

mem.note: let me learn the hard way

effects.log: {npc} comes home three days later, broke, ill and wiser. You make congee.

events.text: {npc} is getting married. {He} asks you to give the blessing at the wedding.

choices.text: Give the blessing and pay for the feast

effects.log: You get three sentences in before your voice breaks. Everyone pretends not to notice.

choices.text: Give your best sword as a wedding gift

effects.log: The sword leaves your house. Something of you goes with it, and that is the point.

events.text: In a friendly spar, {npc} beats you. Fairly. {He} looks frightened, then proud.

mem.note: bowed to me after I won

effects.log: A parent's best day is the day the child wins. {npc} will remember your laugh forever.

mem.note: took me seriously as a fighter

effects.log: You win the rematch, barely. You both know it will not happen again.

events.text: The family house, the fields, the old sword: {npc} wants all of it, and the village is taking sides.

effects.log: You walk away with nothing and a clean heart. Ten years later, {npc} comes to apologise.

choices.text: Split it fairly before the magistrate

effects.log: The magistrate is fair and slow. {npc} does not speak to you for three years.

events.text: Two branches of your family have not spoken in twenty years over a wedding seating plan. A funeral brings them into one room.

effects.log: An hour of terrible silence, then an old joke, then tears. The feud ends over the funeral rice.
The feud continues. It will outlive everyone in the room.

events.text: At the Lantern Festival, a stranger's lantern string tangles with yours, and neither of you lets go first.

mem.note: walked the river with me at the Lantern Festival

effects.log: {npc} talks about the stars, then about everything. (People: spend time together, and perhaps propose.)

mem.note: bowed to me at the festival

effects.log: {npc} smiles and leaves. You look for {him} in the crowd the rest of the night.

events.text: You pull a stranger out of a flooded river. {npc}, dripping, refuses to let you leave without knowing your name.

mem.note: pulled me out of the river

effects.log: Letters arrive at your door for a month. They are very good letters. (People: spend time together, and perhaps propose.)
You become a local legend: the stranger from the river. {npc} keeps looking for you.

events.text: {npc}, a fighter from another sect, beats you in a public bout, then asks you to dinner to make up for it.

mem.note: had dinner with me after our bout

effects.log: Dinner becomes a long walk, which becomes a habit. (People: spend time together, and perhaps propose.)

mem.note: lost to me twice and still came to dinner

effects.log: You lose the rematch too. Then you accept dinner.
